Unargumented it announces 'waiting up to 600s and at least 10 polls'. The 60 s heartbeat fires once: with floor 150 it printed 'still waiting for every process of the run to end: poll 118, 60s of 0s' and then 'timed out after 76s (150 polls)'. judgementOnTheNewTestFile.verdict: Two of its three cases pin behaviour; the third pins the announcement text, and one real way the function could break stays uncovered.
detail: Case 1 ('a poll that costs more than the whole deadline does not end the wait') and case 2 ('a process of the run that never ends fails the wait once the poll floor is reached') pin behaviour, and I proved it rather than asserting it: both mutations I ran — the give-up conjunction turned into a disjunction, and a wait made unable to fail — redden exactly those two cases.

Case 3 ('a call with no arguments waits the production bounds, 600 s and 10 polls') pins the implementation's note text, not its behaviour: it parses the digits out of the first stdout line, so a reworded note that carries another number reddens it for nothing, and the walk it drives clears at poll 1, so the default bounds are never exercised. The behavioural form of the same case drives the unargumented call against a walk that keeps reporting a process and shows that nine polls have not failed it.

One way the function could break that none of the three would catch: a give-up on the poll floor alone, dropping the wall-clock half of the conjunction (`polls >= floor`). Case 1 still returns 0, case 2 still fails at poll 3, case 3 is untouched — yet the wait would then give up after about five seconds on a fast machine where the processes merely linger, which is the deadline's whole purpose. My driver's `5 1` case (floor spent, deadline not: ten polls over five seconds, then the failure) is what pins it; as a case in that file it is `wait("printf '%s\\n' 7777", "5 1")` with `expect(r.calls).toBeGreaterThan(1)` beside the non-zero exit. No red test is written for it here because the shipped function is correct: this is uncovered ground, not a defect, and whether the file grows a fourth case is the architect's call.
